items.title: How to find your arbitrage (from the guy who’s done it 3x)
items.summary: Nick Kokonas reveals how he mastered multiple fields—from options trading and building the world-class restaurant Alinea to creating the software company Tock—by viewing every industry through the lens of time-scale arbitrage, intense daily execution, and adjacent-industry theft.
items.content_text:
### TL;DR
Nick Kokonas reveals how he mastered multiple fields—from options trading and building the world-class restaurant Alinea to creating the software company Tock—by viewing every industry through the lens of time-scale arbitrage, intense daily execution, and adjacent-industry theft.

---

### Trading Floor Origins & The Art of Arbitrage

* **The Reality of High-Stakes Trading:** 
  * **Capital Scarcity:** Nick Kokonas started trading with just $60,000 ($20,000 of his own money and $40,000 from a backer), which he describes as drastically undercapitalized for the floor.
  * **The 1-Year Goal:** Kokonas set a hard target to be trading on a badge within one year of taking a $5.25/hour runner job at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, hitting his goal almost to the day.
  * **Day 1 Trial by Fire:** On his first day in the pits, the strict rule was that he had to complete at least one trade in a zero-sum, hostile, and chaotic physical environment to break the psychological seal.
* **Bypassing the 30-Second Gap:**
  * **The Time-Scale Arb:** Recognizing that a trade execution process took 30 to 40 seconds via paper tickets passed between New York and Chicago, Kokonas sought to bridge the gap directly.
  * **Regulatory Scrutiny:** By meticulously reading the voluminous CFTC rules—which lawyers and board members rarely read in full—he discovered that direct communication between identical firm tax IDs was not explicitly barred.
  * **Union Workarounds:** When the Merc blocked dedicated fiber-optic line permits to protect broker group interests, Kokonas bribed union cable workers with cases of Jameson to run the line.
  * **Peak Revenue:** The direct telecommunications link generated instant, zero-risk arbitrage profits, scaling to over $100 million in trading revenue at its peak.

### Restaurant Innovation & Alinea's Blueprint

* **Open-Sourcing a Masterpiece:**
  * **Building in Public:** Before launching Alinea, Kokonas created the "Alinea Project" forum thread on eGullet, open-sourcing the business plan, name choices, and menu development.
  * **Marketing Leverage:** The public documentation generated hundreds of thousands of views and early demand, securing heavy press coverage from the *New York Times*, *Wall Street Journal*, and *Gourmet Magazine* before opening day.
  * **The Michelin Goal:** The explicit target was to build the best restaurant in America and make it so exceptional that the Michelin Guide (which had not yet expanded to the U.S.) would look bad for omitting it.
* **Operations, Margins, and Scale:**
  * **The Universal Restaurant Calculator:** Kokonas built a single-tab spreadsheet with roughly 80 cells to track every possible cost input, realizing that the low barrier to entry causes most restaurants to fail due to poor business fundamentals.
  * **Financial Success:** Unlike the popular narrative that restaurants only net 2-3%, Alinea scaled to roughly $20 million in annual revenue with 18% to 20% profit margins, ultimately selling in 2023 for an 8x return on initial investment (totaling roughly 27x to 28x overall with quarterly distributions).

### Software & The Tock Revolution

* **Solving the Host Stand:**
  * **The KYC Problem:** Kokonas founded Tock out of frustration with OpenTable, which acted as an intermediary and left restaurants completely blind to who was walking through their doors (Know Your Customer).
  * **Dynamic Pricing:** Tock introduced variable pricing for time-slotted businesses, matching the reality that a Tuesday 9:00 PM table has fundamentally different demand than a Saturday 7:00 PM table.
* **The M&A Playbook:**
  * **Diligence Control:** When selling Tock during COVID-19, Kokonas, along with co-founder Jeff Kaplan and CFO Steve Bernaki, converted an 896-question diligence list into a Google Doc and color-coded it.
  * **Bypassing Intermediaries:** By refusing to act as passive passengers and completing the rigorous data request in just three days, they saved millions in advisory fees while keeping the deal on track to close before the buyer's Q1 S1 filing deadline.

### Stealing from Adjacencies: Magic & Theater

* **Borrowing from Magicians:**
  * **Attention Control:** Instead of reading standard hospitality books, Kokonas studied magic books by authors like Nate Stanforth and Darren Brown to understand how magicians handle attention, sight lines, and audience positioning.
  * **Service Positioning:** Applying magical principles, Alinea servers were trained to stand *alongside* the diner rather than directly across from them, creating a collaborative "same team" dynamic.
* **The "Strange House" Venture:**
  * **Immersive Illusion:** Kokonas partnered with magician Nate Stanforth and game designer Alistair Lee to build *Strange House*—a 90,000-square-foot purpose-built experiential venue beneath Wall Street.
  * **Human Connection:** The project aims to combat societal isolation by leveraging theatrical staging, psychological illusion, and Disney-style room throughput to evoke childlike wonder and foster deep human connection among strangers.

### Notable Quotes

> *"If you wake up every day feeling great, you're not taking enough risk. If you wake up every day throwing up, you're taking too much risk. You need to feel a tingle of uncomfortableness."* — **Nick Kokonas**

> *"Expertise is such a trap... Once you get to expert level, you're screwed because somebody who's younger, hungrier, fresher eyes, more willing to break convention to find the new way through is going to kick your ass. So before your ass gets kicked, you should quit."* — **Nick Kokonas**

> *"Knowing what great is is making mostly [mistakes] 99% of the time... If you want to be a great chef, you show up at 6:00 a.m. and you make 25 sauces."* — **Nick Kokonas**

> *"Intensity is the strategy. I spent a lot of my life searching for the better way, the better strategy, the hack... As I hang out with enough winners, you realize the difference is not that they knew something I didn't know... but like they applied a greater level of intensity to a pretty visible strategy."* — **Shaan Puri**

items.title: Inflation, The Deficit & Why the Dollar Stays King with Benn Steil | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 81
items.summary: Despite persistent inflation, a massive $40 trillion federal deficit, and an aging investor base, the U.S. dollar retains its status as the global financial anchor because there are no viable currency alternatives.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Despite persistent inflation, a massive $40 trillion federal deficit, and an aging investor base, the U.S. dollar retains its status as the global financial anchor because there are no viable currency alternatives.

## The Fed, Inflation, and Rates
- **Inflation Persistence:**
  - On October 14, inflation came in at **3.7%**, exceeding market expectations of **3.6%** and creating pressure on the Federal Reserve.
  - While temporary oil shocks are typically "looked through," the Fed is deeply concerned that delaying action could unmoor longer-term inflation expectations.
- **Federal Reserve Dynamics:**
  - Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh faces an unenviable political and policy bind, caught between a potential majority committee vote for rate hikes and political pressure from Donald Trump.
  - Benn Steil supports the Fed's elimination of formal forward guidance, noting that empirical evidence shows the Fed is systematically worse at forecasting than blue-chip private sector forecasters.
  - Steil defends the Fed's large balance sheet of **$6.5 to $7 trillion**, stating it does not hinder the Fed's ability to control inflation using interest on reserves.

## Fiscal Policy, Scott Bessent, and the Deficit
- **Bessent's Operation Twist:**
  - Treasury official Scott Bessent launched an operation to sell short-term Treasuries and buy long-term Treasuries to the tune of **$6 billion** to lower long-term rates.
  - The market quickly dismissed the move, calculating that **$6 billion** represents just **0.016%** of the **$40 trillion** national debt.
- **The U.S. Deficit & Crowding Out:**
  - The U.S. federal deficit currently runs at about **6% of GDP annually**, totaling **$40 trillion**.
  - The trajectory is concerning due to a crowding-out effect: Treasury is competing globally for capital against booming AI infrastructure investments, pushing interest rates upward.
  - Congress and the executive branch currently lack the serious political will to cut spending or address entitlement reform.

## The Global Dollar Standard & The France Sovereign Debt Crisis
- **The Exorbitant Privilege:**
  - Historically, 76% of the market for U.S. debt consisted of "rate-insensitive investors" (mostly central banks holding Treasuries as a reflex).
  - That figure has dropped to **43%**, meaning the U.S. must increasingly attract rate-sensitive investors, creating an accelerationist effect on interest rate rises as deficits grow.
- **The Lack of Alternatives:**
  - The U.S. dollar remains dominant simply as the "winner of an ugly dog contest"; no major fiat alternative exists.
  - Central banks (particularly China and Russia) have increasingly diversified into gold and repatriated reserves to protect themselves against aggressive U.S. dollar-based financial sanctions (such as those applied to Iran).
- **France's Vulnerability:**
  - France faces an even uglier fiscal position than the U.S. with large deficits and zero political will for reform (e.g., Marine Le Pen's proposal to lower the retirement age from **62 to 60**).
  - Unlike U.S. Treasuries, no bank or sovereign wealth fund globally holds French sovereign bonds on reflex; French debt is treated strictly like corporate risk.

## Historical Counterfactuals: Henry Wallace, Bretton Woods, and the Cold War
- **The Henry Wallace Counterfactual:**
  - In Henry Steil's book *The World That Wasn't*, he explores the counterfactual where Henry Wallace (FDR's third-term Vice President) succeeded a failing Roosevelt instead of Harry Truman.
  - Wallace, despite not being an ideological spy, was a Soviet fellow traveler who praised Soviet economic planning and would have opposed the Truman Doctrine, the Marshall Plan, the creation of West Germany, and NATO.
- **Bretton Woods & Harry Dexter White:**
  - The 1944 Bretton Woods conference established the IMF, the World Bank, and the dollar-based international financial system.
  - The U.S. architect of the system, Treasury official Harry Dexter White, was later identified in FBI files (via 18 intercepted Soviet intelligence cables) as a Soviet asset who actively protected other agents and undermined U.S. policy (such as giving currency plates to the Soviets, which cost the U.S. Treasury about **$8 billion** in today's dollars).
- **The Marshall Plan:**
  - Following WWII, the IMF and World Bank were largely mothballed through the 1950s, making the Marshall Plan the primary vehicle for rehabilitating war-torn Europe and countering Soviet expansionism.

## Notable Quotes
> "The best way I've heard the US dollar described is as the winner of an ugly dog contest. That you can only compare this particular dog to the rest of the dogs that are out there in the competition."
> — **Benn Steil**

> "If you're running a firm, you know that when you calculate what your profit's going to be, you multiply the price of your product and the number of products you're going to sell. If you smash your products so you you can't sell them, obviously you make no revenue whatsoever."
> — **Steve Eisman** *(discussing Henry Wallace's agricultural policies)*

> "The last thing Kevin Warsh wants is to be a dissenting vote in a committee he supposedly leads as chairman. Um but he also doesn't want to infuriate the man who appointed him, Donald Trump."
> — **Benn Steil**

items.title: Palantir & Ondas | Introducing Regna AI: Sovereign AI for Defense | Episode 3
items.summary: Regna AI is a new sovereign AI joint venture between Palantir and Ondas designed to provide mission-specific, post-trained open-weights models for defense, intelligence, and edge operations while safeguarding sensitive data.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Regna AI is a new sovereign AI joint venture between Palantir and Ondas designed to provide mission-specific, post-trained open-weights models for defense, intelligence, and edge operations while safeguarding sensitive data.

## Origins and Vision of Regna AI
* **Founding Context:** 
  * Formed after six months of close collaboration between Ondas and Palantir, tackling mission autonomy capabilities like *Sky Weaver*.
  * The name *Regna* translates to "Sovereign Kingdom," reflecting the commitment to delivering sovereign AI solutions for defense and government customers.
* **The Sovereign AI Thesis:** 
  * Inspired by Palantir CEO Dr. Alex Karp’s vision for sovereign AI across industries.
  * Focuses on post-training models for specific missions (such as intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, or ISR) to compound operational "alpha"—measured in lives saved rather than commercial metrics.
* **Spin-Out Structure:** 
  * Initially bootstrapped by Ondas with Ondas serving as the first customer.
  * Structured to operate as an independent company serving the broader defense ecosystem rather than just a proprietary internal tool.

## Technical Architecture & Edge Constraints
* **Rejection of General-Purpose AI:** 
  * Rather than relying on cloud-hosted frontier models designed for general tasks, Regna AI builds specialized, fine-tuned models tailored to specific operational constraints.
* **Edge Deployment:** 
  * Models are engineered to run on limited form factors and compute footprints found on edge platforms, including stratospheric balloons, long-endurance UAVs, and ground robotics.
* **Disconnected Operations:** 
  * Designed for environments with limited bandwidth and compute, enabling distributed inferencing directly on platforms while maintaining situational awareness.

## Human-in-the-Loop Validation and Trust
* **Forward-Deployed Engineering Model:** 
  * Utilizes Palantir-style Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) working shoulder-to-shoulder with customers to map data inputs directly to operational decisions.
* **"Mini-Labs" for Customers:** 
  * Commanders maintain continuous control over model training, reviewing end-to-end data pipelines and recommended actions.
  * Operators can iteratively accept or reject outputs, ensuring high trust before deploying models to the battlefield or simulated exercises.

## Complex Multi-Domain Use Cases
* **Stratospheric Balloon Routing:** 
  * Managing infinitely complex operations for stratospheric balloons—including dynamic weather, wind patterns, exclusion zones, and inclement weather routing.
* **Multi-Domain Orchestration:** 
  * Connecting assets across the stratosphere, air, space, ground, and surface domains to distill infinite data streams into actionable commander decisions.
* **Building on Existing Frameworks:** 
  * Leverages prior operational learnings from *Sky Weaver*, mission control, and orbit systems to shape the architecture of the new models.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The alpha that we create for Ondas through our partnership with Palantir is through some of the work we're doing and some of the agentic AI through Sky Weaver, but we're talking about saving lives, protecting lives around the world, through some of our intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance systems. And in my mind, the alpha that is created is how many lives can you save?"* — Ryan Hartman

> *"When we think about building software for our customers at Palantir, we're always, we're never building general-purpose software. We're building software that works for the customer where the customer is at and where the problems are at."* — Eashan Panjwani

> *"They're not going to be guessing as to where the data is going, they're not going to have to wonder what is biasing a decision that comes out of the model because they're the ones that are going to be saying, 'I like that output, I don't like that output, so let's make it more like the one that I did like.'"* — Ryan Hartman

items.title: The $2B AI Startup Simulating Human Behavior with 85% Accuracy
items.summary: Simile is a $2B AI startup building foundation models of human behavior through digital twins, backed by $300M in total funding from Greenoaks, Index Ventures, Fei-Fei Li, and Andrej Karpathy.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Simile is a $2B AI startup building foundation models of human behavior through digital twins, backed by $300M in total funding from Greenoaks, Index Ventures, Fei-Fei Li, and Andrej Karpathy. By combining large language models with agentic architectures and partnerships with over 40 million real people globally, the company’s technology has demonstrated 85%+ accuracy in predicting human behavior and is currently used by enterprises like CVS, Wealthfront, Deloitte, and Banco Itaú to simulate decisions before real-world deployment.

## Origins & Research Evolution: From "Smallville" to Foundation Models
* **Academic Origins:** The company evolved from *Smallville*, a 2023 research experiment led at Stanford by Joon Sung Park and co-founders Michael Bernstein and Percy Liang.
* **The Smallville Experiment:** 
  * A game town (resembling Pokemon or Sims) populated by 25 autonomous AI agents powered by GPT-3/3.5 paired with an agentic architecture featuring memory, planning, and reflection.
  * Agents performed daily routines, organized a Valentine's Day party, and formed relationships with zero pre-programmed scripts, demonstrating emergent behavior.
* **Core Breakthrough:** Proved that foundational LLMs could be prompted to generate novel, human-like behaviors and interact within simulated communities.

## Technology, Methodology & Validation
* **Individual and Environmental Modeling:** Simula models individuals first (learning base traits like risk tolerance and aesthetics) and then places them into simulated environments to observe chaotic, emergent societal interactions.
* **The "Gap" in Human Behavior:** 
  * Surveys show normal distributions (what people *say* they will do, e.g., going to the gym).
  * Actual behavior follows an exponential curve driven by activation energy and "optionality" (opportunity costs and available alternatives).
* **Validation & Accuracy:** 
  * Early testing relied on human evaluators assessing agent believability ("illusion of life").
  * Scaled to a representative sample of 1,000 U.S. participants using voice-to-voice AI interviews to build digital twins, predicting actual behavior with 85%+ accuracy after a two-week blind test.
* **Data Quality Controls:** Partnered with Gallup (holding a panel of hundreds of thousands built over decades) and implemented attention checks (arithmetic, recall) and sparse polling intervals to prevent respondent fatigue and gaming.
* **Informed Consent:** Excludes underage populations and unconsenting individuals; otherwise aims for a complete representative snapshot of society, capturing both positive and negative human tendencies.

## Business Model, Products & Enterprise Use Cases
* **Platform Offering:** Delivered via a SaaS web interface where enterprise users define target populations and ask unlimited questions to receive instant simulations with an accompanying confidence score (0-100 range probability, akin to a scientific p-value).
* **Vertical-Specific Agent Banks:** Maintains pre-built simulated panels across key verticals, supplemented by custom data collection reaching tens to hundreds of thousands of real people weekly (with a 24-hour turnaround for new panels).
* **Key Enterprise Customers:** 
  * **Retailers:** CVS (optimizing store layout, messaging, and decor).
  * **Financial Institutions:** Wealthfront, Deloitte, and Banco Itaú (Brazil) for testing policies and communicating corporate values.
  * **Other Verticals:** Entertainment, CPG, and automotive companies.
* **High-Stakes Use Cases:** Concept testing, conjoint analysis, max-diff analysis, messaging optimization for electric vehicles, internal HR retention modeling, and recruitment strategy.

## Team Composition & Company Operations
* **Team Scale:** Approximately 100 employees split across science/modeling (20–25%), engineering/product (including talent from DoorDash), and a heavily for-deployed go-to-market motion led by co-founder Laney Yellen.
* **Academic Roots:** Roughly 20% of the team consists of labmates and academic relatives from Stanford's computer science department.
* **Investor Base:** Backed by Greenoaks, Index Ventures, Fei-Fei Li, Andrej Karpathy, and Percy Liang, alongside angel investors drawn to the inevitability of social simulation.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Industry Maturity Timeline:** Joon Sung Park predicts that the simulation industry will reach the maturity level where the coding agent industry is today within **1.5 to 2 years**.

## Notable Quotes
> "The best way to understand something is to recreate it... Simulation is a lot like creating a portrait of who we are as a society."
> — Joon Sung Park

> "People are actually not that interested in predicting the future... if I told you that your market is going to crash in two quarters, they're all going to then ask, 'What do we need to do now to change that?' But it's always that second part that matters more: so what do we need to do now to shape the future?"
> — Joon Sung Park

> "These are people whose greatest prize in winning the current game is gaining the right an invitation to play the next game."
> — Joon Sung Park

items.title: The New Full-Stack Designer
items.summary: Marvin Schwaibold of Shopify and Aaron Epstein of Y Combinator review how AI tooling is shifting product design toward a full-stack, editor-driven workflow, and evaluate motion and interactivity across five viewer-submitted startup websites.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Marvin Schwaibold of Shopify and Aaron Epstein of Y Combinator review how AI tooling is shifting product design toward a full-stack, editor-driven workflow, and evaluate motion and interactivity across five viewer-submitted startup websites.

## Shopify's AI Product Studio & Workflow Evolution
* **Shift to AI-Driven Workflows:** **Marvin Schwaibold** explains that while design processes remain iterative, tooling has moved from static aesthetic layouts in Figma to terminal-based AI agents (like Codex and Cloud Code) that rapidly produce real, testable demos.
* **The Designer as Editor:** **Marvin Schwaibold** notes that AI handles the heavy lifting of code and execution complexity, placing humans in the driving seat to curate, quality-control, and steer outputs based on what looks and feels right.
* **Shopify's Dual-Track Initiative:** **Marvin Schwaibold** describes his team's work over the past year touching core surfaces, split into two areas:
  * **Admin Experience:** Redesigning and polishing interfaces for web and the mobile app (the "green app").
  * **Sidekick:** Building AI infrastructure that allows merchants to manage and automate their stores conversationally via chat.
* **Prototyping for Buy-In:** **Marvin Schwaibold** emphasizes that tangible prototypes built with AI spread through an organization like wildfire and secure founder/executive alignment much faster than traditional PRD documents.

## Independent Studio Roots & The "Primal" System
* **Molly Studio Background:** **Marvin Schwaibold** highlights his time running the Brooklyn design studio Molly alongside partner J Tal, working with major clients like Collins, Apple, and Google with a tight team of two to three concurrent clients.
* **The Primal Content System:** **Marvin Schwaibold** explains this structured methodology used to digest heavy client information into exploratory website flows where content is progressively disclosed rather than demanding attention.
* **Collins Bookshelf Craft:** **Marvin Schwaibold** details a hand-crafted bookshelf component built with engineer Jesper featuring organic, level-up bounce animations designed as an "Easter egg" to signal agency-level dedication and craft to potential clients.
* **Joining Shopify:** **Marvin Schwaibold** shares that Tobi Lutke’s mandate—stating that the future needs to be designed and requiring designers to paint a picture—inspired him to bring his studio into Shopify for massive-scale impact.

## Grass Shader & DialKit Prototyping
* **Weekend Grass Shader Project:** **Marvin Schwaibold** details a personal project (available on GitHub via MarvinSchwaibold/grass-shader) converting real grass video footage into a web shader with 217,000 individual grass blade variations.
* **Iterative AI Prompting:** **Marvin Schwaibold** describes feeding video, screenshots, and topographical height maps into ChatGPT and Codex agents over multiple prompts to correct underlying terrain geometry and lighting.
* **DialKit Integration:** **Marvin Schwaibold** explains how Josh introduced **DialKit** (run via `npm run` from the website) to add binary toggles and variable sliders, exposing underlying structures to instantly spot errors and tweak values like grass length and wind movement.
* **Carousel Iteration:** **Marvin Schwaibold** shares that a portfolio carousel inspired by Mike Matas took 91 prompts to get right, utilizing a side parameter panel to dial in physical properties like "pull boost."

## Viewer Website Reviews (Motion & Interactivity)
* **Nstack:** **Marvin Schwaibold** and **Aaron Epstein** praise the retro, whimsical desktop-emulator feel and dropping users straight into the product, but criticize visual overload, dense sidebars, and competing CTA buttons that violate the rule of clear visual hierarchy.
* **SkillSync:** **Marvin Schwaibold** and **Aaron Epstein** note that while dark mode and dark aesthetic are clean, the page is a "mile wide and an inch deep," burying key information behind unclicked sidebar tabs and utilizing superfluous animations that do not aid user comprehension.
* **Instaplay:** **Aaron Epstein** and **Marvin Schwaibold** highlight the instant engagement of interactive prompt-to-game capabilities, but critique the immediate paywall/sign-up friction and hidden navigation paths that obscure the primary goal of creating games.
* **Netlify (Mentlify):** **Marvin Schwaibold** and **Aaron Epstein** praise the clean, trustworthy presentation, reductive typography, strong social proof (Microsoft, Anthropic, Coinbase), and breathable, well-spaced chapter-based scroll flow.
* **Nullify:** **Aaron Epstein** and **Marvin Schwaibold** commend the high-quality instructional videos, but criticize the competing headline placeholders, difficult click targets on carousels, and the use of sluggish scroll-jacking that hinders native user scroll speed.
* **Instinct:** **Aaron Epstein** and **Marvin Schwaibold** praise the immersive 3D/video elements and brave serif font choices for space tech, but recommend instantly triggering hover states and adopting **Blossom Carousel** (from the open-source Blossom Carousel GitHub repo) for smoother trackpad scrolling.

## Notable Quotes
> "We're more the editors now than ever before... AI is definitely raised the ceiling for all of us, but it's not a crafter. It can execute complexity... but it doesn't know what looks good and what looks bad and that's for me to decide."
> — *Marvin Schwaibold*

> "Smooth scrolling on websites is a disaster in the industry... You want interruptible software because our thought patterns are interruptible... You would never want to get a user into an environment where they have to smooth scroll or scroll jack through the content."
> — *Marvin Schwaibold*

> "Codex won't get mad at me if I need 91 approaches at getting the animation correct. If I had done that with my engineer, they would probably flip out."
> — *Marvin Schwaibold*

items.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent to Iran International: Iran’s economy to shrink by over 25%
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent detailed the ongoing "Operation Economic Outcast" against Iran, predicting a 25%+ contraction in Iran's economy by March 2027 and advising Iranian citizens to hoard fuel and withhold taxes.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent detailed the ongoing "Operation Economic Outcast" against Iran, predicting a 25%+ contraction in Iran's economy by March 2027 and advising Iranian citizens to hoard fuel and withhold taxes. Bessent stated that the US naval blockade is airtight, regional financial nodes are being systematically severed, and the Trump administration remains resolute regardless of US midterm elections.

## Campaign Status & Economic Impact
- **Operation Outcast Progress:** Launched roughly 8 weeks ago as an escalation of the maximum pressure campaign initiated in March 2025.
- **Inflation & Currency:** Inflation has surpassed 100%, and the regime has reportedly stopped publishing the true value of the rial, which Bessent estimates is trading around 3 million to the dollar.
- **Global Compliance:** 
  - Several Gulf countries have severed financial ties.
  - Mahan Air has halted all flights except to Russia and China; other airlines defying restrictions face imminent shutdown by Treasury.
- **Humanitarian Channels:** 
  - Treasury maintains open humanitarian channels for food and medicine, but Bessent noted the regime is too broke to pay for international imports due to lack of dollars.
  - The central bank continues printing money, driving inflation while failing to pay government salaries.

## Cracking Down on International Financial Networks
- **Targeting Trustees & Brokers:** 
  - Treasury is targeting trade and financial facilitators operating from Dubai to Hong Kong.
  - Many trustees are refusing to return funds to Tehran, viewing the regime as a bankrupt entity.
- **International Banking Interventions:** 
  - Treasury has subpoenaed a Greek bank, sent information requests to six European banks, and targeted institutions across Pakistan, Dubai, Egypt, Turkey, and Russia.
  - Specific actions include shutting Dubai branches of an Egyptian bank, closing a Turkish bank, and targeting VTB (the second-largest Russian bank) for aiding the regime.
- **Cryptocurrency & Asset Tracking:** 
  - The regime's use of digital currencies is viewed as an act of desperation.
  - Treasury is tracking and escrowing illicit crypto and luxury assets (such as expensive apartments) to recover funds intended for the Iranian people.
- **Whistleblower Rewards:** 
  - Treasury offers a whistleblower program where citizens, diaspora members, and embassy employees can claim up to 30% of recovered regime funds by reporting illicit channels via the Treasury website.
  - Sanitization and un-sanctioning are offered to brokers who come forward and cooperate.

## Naval Blockade & Energy Sector Collapse
- **Strait of Hormuz Control:** 
  - The US Navy controls the strait, refuting regime claims. 
  - Energy is flowing out nightly at rates exceeding pre-war levels.
- **Oil & Gasoline Shortages:** 
  - Iran has effectively "no oil on the water" and zero loadings at Kharg Island.
  - Domestic gasoline production is faltering in a country with the world's third-largest energy assets.
- **Military Neutralization:** 
  - Iran's navy and air force have been neutralized.
  - Substantial missile and drone stockpiles were destroyed, alongside 85% of Iranian missile factories.

## Political Isolation & Regime Dynamics
- **Internal Fractures:** 
  - Economic pressure is causing visible infighting among politicians, the IRGC, and the Supreme Leader.
  - Public figures (such as President, Speaker Ghalibaf, and the head of the central bank) have issued economic warnings over the summer, followed by some IRGC members.
- **Leadership Isolation:** 
  - Bessent characterized IRGC commanders as "rats in a sewer pipe" hiding in deep locations and remaining blind to the suffering of ordinary Iranians.
- **Midterm Election Calculus:** 
  - Bessent dismissed regime hopes that upcoming US midterm elections would shift Washington's calculus, stating President Trump's resolute blockade and policies remain entirely unchanged.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Economic Contraction:** Scott Bessent predicts that Iran's economy will contract by more than 25% between March 2026 and March 2027 — a contraction exceeding that of the Soviet Union after its collapse.
- **Campaign Intensity:** Scott Bessent claims that the next eight weeks of Operation Economic Outcast will become "even more intense."
- **Advice to Citizens:** Scott Bessent advises Iranian citizens to stop paying taxes and immediately stock up on heating fuel and gasoline ahead of an impending winter shortage.

## Notable Quotes
> "I would predict that for from March of 26 until March of 27 the economy would contract more than 25% which is more than the Soviet Union contracted after uh its collapse."  
> — **Secretary Scott Bessent**

> "My advice to the Iranian people would be don't pay your taxes because you're not going to get anything back from the government. They're going to keep cutting social benefits."  
> — **Secretary Scott Bessent**

> "There has never been anything uh this powerful before. The kinetic wartime action... The blockade is the airtight, watertight. Nothing is coming in or out."  
> — **Secretary Scott Bessent**

items.title: Why OpenAI Is Racing to Make Computer Use Superhuman
items.summary: OpenAI's computer-using agents, supercharged by the Astra model, are now faster than average humans at operating software and entering a massive scaling phase across consumer and enterprise markets.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
OpenAI's computer-using agents, supercharged by the Astra model, are now faster than average humans at operating software and entering a massive scaling phase across consumer and enterprise markets. Led by OpenAI's Ari Weinstein and James Sun, the company is tackling enterprise adoption through deterministic sandboxes and human-in-the-loop controls, while driving consumer adoption through proactive "dots" and universal web navigation.

## Astra Model Capabilities & Performance
* **Speed and Efficiency:**
  * **Faster Execution:** Ari Weinstein noted that Astra is faster on average than previous models because it uses fewer thinking tokens to accomplish the same tasks.
  * **Approaching Superhuman:** The models are now faster than the average human at using a computer and are getting extremely close to being faster than expert human users.
  * **Video Game Benchmarks:** Internally, Astra plays video games against older models like `5.6` and wins every time, successfully beating games like *Fallout* in roughly 30 hours.
* **Reliability and Creative Work:**
  * **Edge Reliability:** Reliability has increased in hard-to-perceive ways that matter significantly in practice, moving from roughly 97% to 99% reliability.
  * **Creative Tasks:** Excels at creative work, such as drawing things in Microsoft Paint during live voice interactions.
* **Alignment and Security:**
  * **Enhanced Safety:** James Sun highlighted that Astra is OpenAI's most aligned model, featuring system cards showing much better resistance to prompt injections and unintended actions.
  * **Enterprise Trust:** This alignment makes it significantly safer for sensitive enterprise use cases like procurement and vendor/customer communications.

## Enterprise Automation & Legacy Software
* **Boring Opportunities in Systems of Record:**
  * **Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP):** Automates complex legacy software that lacks APIs and has been used for 15 to 20 years.
  * **Procurement Workflows:** Replaces giant spreadsheets (e.g., ordering lab equipment) and manual ops data-entry with automated end-to-end purchasing and vendor outreach.
  * **Finance Reconciliation:** Operates financial software and multiple ledgers at month-end to reconcile expenses without needing custom APIs.
  * **Sales & CRM:** Gathers prospecting data and inputs records across disparate sales software and CRM systems.
* **Vertical Industry Adoption:**
  * **Restaurant Group Example:** Software uses back-storage photos and vision to project traffic, automate grocery ordering via platforms like Shopee, and adjust employee timetables in ERP systems based on historical data.

## Enterprise Controls & Guardrails
* **Deterministic Sandboxes:**
  * **Application and URL Restrictions:** Enterprise admins can create a sandbox around the agent to deterministically restrict which apps, websites, and data sources it can access.
* **Human-in-the-Loop Dials:**
  * **Auto-Approve System ("Guardian"):** A smart model evaluates every agent action to decide if it is safe and aligned.
  * **Custom Intervention Levels:** Enterprises can dial in specific requirements—such as mandating human approval for file downloads, uploads, or visits to new websites.
* **Design & Trust Building:**
  * **Visual Cues:** Features a visible cursor (affectionately called the "Codex cursor" by the team) and fun animations so users can watch the agent perform tasks cleanly and transparently.

## Consumer Use Cases, "Dots," & Proactivity
* **Automating Drudgery:**
  * **Daily Tasks:** Fills out DMV forms, unsubscribes from email lists, organizes personal finance spreadsheets, and manages meal planning.
* **Cloud Computers and "Dots":**
  * **Dedicated Cloud Environments:** Users can spin up "dots," each getting its own cloud computer and full web browser to execute tasks.
  * **Proactive Interventions:** James Sun shared how dots proactively catch missed calendar invites from external Gmail emails and monitor Slack channels to surface critical feedback and parse Sentry logs.
* **Consumer Growth & Form Factors:**
  * **YC-Level Growth:** Following the integration of browser use into existing products, OpenAI has seen YC-level week-over-week growth.
  * **Mobile Expansion:** The next inflection point involves bringing powerful cloud computing and agentic workflows to mobile devices for billions of everyday users.

## The Future of Software: Legacy vs. AI-Native
* **Coexistence of Legacy and New Software:**
  * **Prolonging Legacy Systems:** Because computer use interacts with software the same way a human does (via UI rather than APIs), it extends the utility of 10-to-40-year-old legacy software.
  * **New Software Standards:** Standards like **WebMCP** are being adopted in in-app browsers, allowing agents and humans to share the interface collaboratively (e.g., agents doing tedious work while humans handle final transactions).
* **Hyper-Personalized Software:**
  * **Micro-Applications:** The low cost and complexity of creating software means future applications can be custom-tailored for 100 people or even a single individual (such as custom tactical trainers built for family members).
  * **Shared Intelligence Layers:** The vision points toward coherent user experiences where applications, browsers, and cloud agents share context rather than operating as isolated silos.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Software Interoperability:** "All the software is going to work with agents by default and I think webmcp is a great example of this and I think we'll see more stuff like that." — Ari Weinstein
* **UI Evolution:** "I expect both of those things to continue for a long time... I don't think that that stuff's [legacy software] going to go away overnight." — Ari Weinstein
* **The Scaling Moment:** "I think we're at the scaling moment of computer use both for consumer and enterprise. Yeah. At the same time." — James Sun

## Notable Quotes
> "We've gotten computer use now to a place where it's faster than the average human. And I think we're getting really close where it is superhuman."
> — Ari Weinstein

> "Computer use is not like a thing you pick up and just say I want to do something with it. It's really like the universal kind of API that the model has to do whatever it takes."
> — James Sun

> "Humans are so hardwired for direct manipulation. You really want to be able to, you know, move and and and do things with your own hands."
> — Ari Weinstein

items.title: AI Agents Could Drive 10,000x More Web Activity | Former Twitter CEO
items.summary: AI agents could drive 5,000x to 10,000x more web activity than humans, fundamentally transforming the internet from a reactive pull model to a proactive push model.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
AI agents could drive 5,000x to 10,000x more web activity than humans, fundamentally transforming the internet from a reactive pull model to a proactive push model. Parag Agrawal, former Twitter CEO & CTO and current Founder & CEO of Parallel Web Systems, is building the search infrastructure for this agent-first internet, which recently closed a $100 million Series B at a $2 billion valuation.

---

## Parallel Web Systems & Agent-Driven Infrastructure
- **Company Scale & Funding:** 
  - Raised a **$100 million Series B funding round** last month, valuing the AI startup at **$2 billion**.
  - Total reported and announced funding stands at **$230 million**.
  - Team grew **4x this year**, expanding from **30 to 120 employees** (largely driven by building out a Go-To-Market and sales team over the last 3-6 months).
- **Core Product & Integration:**
  - Builds a collection of APIs that AI agents use to search and access the web.
  - Recently shipped an integration powering search in **Browserbase**.
  - Serves prominent customers including **Harvey** (trusted by 80% of AmLaw 100 and >20% of Fortune 500) and **Notion**.
- **Search Architecture Evolution:**
  - Traditional search is memory and CPU-bound; Parallel rearchitects search to be GPU-underpinned and token-efficient.
  - High-signal search allows models to do half the number of searches, using fewer tokens and resulting in cheaper, faster end-to-end applications.
  - Latency requirements for voice agents demand web search results in **150 to 200 milliseconds** (compared to human sub-second products at 600-700 ms).

## The Macro Shift: Agent Web Activity & GPUs
- **Agent Traffic vs. Human Traffic:**
  - Automated agent traffic on the web is "ripping," but actual agent utilization is estimated at **10% to 20% of humans**.
  - Assuming Parag's personal agent usage (several thousand searches per day) becomes mainstream, there is an estimated **5,000x to 10,000x growth** remaining.
- **GPU Sourcing & Infrastructure:**
  - Parallel rents GPUs at scale to meet search traffic demands.
  - The GPU market is characterized by complex physical requirements (placement within 5 milliseconds of a web index) and informal sourcing channels (coordinating availability via iMessage).

## The Economic & Business Model Crisis of the Web
- **Breakdown of Traditional Models:**
  - Traditional monetization (subscription paywalls, human-viewed display ads, affiliate actions) relies on humans "random walking" the web.
  - Because buying actions remain but attention monetization breaks, ad networks and perceived subscription models are not durable.
- **Parallel's Compensation Solution:**
  - Built a system running a model to compute how much to pay each content owner every time an agent reads their content.
  - Acts as a modern "AdSense" equivalent to provide content owners financial incentive and keep the web open.

## Cybersecurity, Safety, and Team Building
- **Security Risks:**
  - Cyber security risks are real, with agents assisting both attackers and defenders.
  - Adversarial threats exist at every layer: web ingestion (injection attacks), model weights, and application builders.
- **Hiring & Talent Density:**
  - Focuses on hiring outliers, noting that "If you don't hire outliers, you don't get outliers."
  - Operates globally with a team that scaled rapidly to 120 people to meet enterprise demand.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Inference-to-Search Ratio:** "For every 10 GPUs the world spends on model inference, we'll spend one to two on web search." — Parag Agrawal
- **Web Transition Timeline:** The internet will transition from reactive pull to hyper-proactive push as agent intelligence costs decrease and always-on agents set up high-precision alerts across the trillion-page web. — Parag Agrawal
- **Agent Growth Trajectory:** Agent usage of the web will experience another 5,000x to 10,000x increase from current baseline levels as adoption spreads globally. — Parag Agrawal

---

## Notable Quotes
> "I was the lunatic walking around 3 years ago telling people agents will use the web a thousand times more than humans ever have... turns out today if you force me, 1,000x is too low a number."
> — **Parag Agrawal**

> "The web is the is a dangerous place... So almost every layer has to obsess about this problem. You can't say oh models will solve it. We have to really focus on it to solve it at our layer before we get into the models."
> — **Parag Agrawal**

> "I only want jobs which I wouldn't hire myself for. So, I want somehow to feel that someone's thrown me into a challenge that on paper I'm not supposed to be able to accomplish."
> — **Parag Agrawal**
