items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Jensen Huang announced major European AI economy investments and unveiled next-generation hardware and software—including the Vera Rubin architecture, DSX POD turnkey AI factories, OpenShell security for autonomous agents, and the RTX Spark personal AI computer.

## European AI Economy & Infrastructure
* **33-Year European Roots:** **Jensen Huang** noted NVIDIA's deep history in Europe, manufacturing early chips (NV1-NV3) in Crolles, France, assembling them in Malta, and partnering with German workstation pioneer Elsa and automotive leaders Audi and Mercedes.
* **$10B European Investment:** **Jensen Huang** announced that NVIDIA has invested nearly $10 billion in Europe over the past year across startups, large partnerships, and 14 newly announced startups during his current tour of France, the UK, Sweden, and Germany.
* **AI Factory Economics & Buildout:** **Jensen Huang** highlighted that a single 1-gigawatt AI factory costs approximately $50 billion (land, power, shell, cooling, compute), generating tens of billions in annual revenue, where a 3-month deployment delay costs up to $10 billion in lost revenue.
* **NVIDIA DSX POD:** **Jensen Huang** introduced the DSX POD, a factory-built, integrated system containing seven liquid-cooled Vera Rubin NVL72 compute racks and 17 kilometers of Spectrum-X cables, reducing on-site installation time from 4–5 months down to about a month.
* **Energy, Cooling, and Efficiency:** **Jensen Huang** detailed that DSX features closed-loop liquid cooling handling up to 45°C coolant temperatures, saving up to 54 million liters of water daily at a 2-gigawatt scale.

## Hardware & Architecture: Vera Rubin & Networking
* **Six Generations of Extreme Co-Design:** **Jensen Huang** contrasted NVIDIA's architecture with Moore's Law (which has largely ended), stating that extreme co-design across chips, systems, software, and algorithms has increased AI performance by 1 million times over the last 10 years.
* **Vera Rubin Architecture:** **Jensen Huang** stated that Vera Rubin is in full production, delivering 100% liquid cooling (reducing assembly time from 2 hours to under 5 minutes per node), 20 petaflops per GPU, and a 30x performance leap over Blackwell in just two years.
* **Networking & Silicon Photonics:** **Jensen Huang** introduced Spectralmax, the world's first co-packaged optics (CPO) solution developed with TSMC using CoWoS technology, featuring a 512-port, 200 gigabits-per-second Ethernet switch that connects lasers directly to the chip without PCB transmission loss.

## Autonomous Agents & OpenShell Security
* **The Five Elements of AI Agents:** **Jensen Huang** defined an agentic system by five core building blocks: the **Model** (perception, reasoning, planning), the **Harness** (exoskeleton/orchestration), the **Sandbox** (isolation environment), **Knowledge** (structured/unstructured data), and **Tools** (CUDA-X simulation and execution).
* **NVIDIA OpenShell & Sentry:** **Jensen Huang** introduced OpenShell (an Apache 2.0 open-source secure runtime enforcing policies at system-call, file-access, and network levels) and NVIDIA Sentry (hardware-isolated monitoring running on BlueField-4 that can quarantine compromised agents in milliseconds).
* **Knowledge Foundation:** **Jensen Huang** outlined NVIDIA's knowledge libraries—including Nemotron Parse, Nemotron Embed, Nemotron Rerank, and Kumo—designed to bridge unstructured PDFs and structured SQL databases to power domain-specific enterprise agents.

## Personal AI & Physical Robotics
* **RTX Spark Personal Computer:** **Jensen Huang** announced the RTX Spark, a 4-year collaboration with Microsoft featuring the N1X chip, delivering 1 petaflops of compute and 128 gigabytes of memory in a laptop/desktop form factor starting at the end of the year.
* **DGX Station with RTX Spark:** **Jensen Huang** introduced the DGX Station workstation variant running Windows, offering 20 petaflops and 754 gigabytes of memory.
* **Robotic Ecosystem & Hyperion Standard:** **Jensen Huang** announced that Volkswagen Vans, JLR, Volvo, and next-generation Mercedes fleets will adopt the Hyperion autonomous vehicle architecture, and unveiled the NVIDIA Agile One reference robot (built with Agile Robotics) launching in Q1 of next year.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* "Every single Telco in the future, with 100,000 sites, representing some 100 gigawatts of distributed Telco base stations and data centers, will in the future evolve into a distributed AI network." — Jensen Huang

## Notable Quotes
> "Artificial intelligence will affect everything we build, and in fact enable us to build new things. In this way, because everyone will use it, every company will be powered by it... like the electricity, it is a new industrial revolution."
> — Jensen Huang

> "Today, the only thing stopping an agent from misusing all that is asking it nicely. Please don't delete anything. Please don't push to main. Please don't touch my SSH keys... But hope isn't security. Safety isn't an aspiration. It's technology and engineering."
> — Jensen Huang

## TL;DR
Jensen Huang delivered the Nvidia GTC Berlin 2026 keynote, announcing a nearly $10 billion investment in Europe over the past year to build out the region's AI economy. He introduced major technological advancements, including the Vera Rubin architecture, the DSX POD supply-chain integration, and the RTX Spark personal AI workstation line.

## Europe's AI Economy and Investments
* **Capital Deployment:** **Jensen Huang** noted that Nvidia has invested nearly $10 billion across European startups and big and small partnerships over the past last year alone.
* **Partnership Ecosystem:** **Jensen Huang** stated that Nvidia now counts over 12,000 partnerships across Europe, working toward the new industrial revolution.
* **Regional Infrastructure:** **Jensen Huang** highlighted European cloud and infrastructure builders, including Mistral in France, Nebius, Schneider Electric, Siemens Energy, and Firebird (a cloud provider in the Central Asia region).

## Vera Rubin Architecture and Full-Stack Hardware
* **Generational Leap:** **Jensen Huang** presented the Vera Rubin architecture in full production, noting it achieves performance 30 times greater than Blackwell in large language model processing in just two years.
* **Vera Computer & CPU:** **Jensen Huang** introduced the Vera CPU featuring eight instructions per clock, the world's first LPDDR memory system, and the fastest on-chip fabric in the world.
* **Spectrum-X Co-Packaged Optics (CPO):** **Jensen Huang** detailed the world's first CPO switch—a 512-port at 200 gigabits per second Ethernet switch—utilizing CoWoS technology created with TSMC to attach silicon photonics directly onto the chip.
* **DSX POD Supply-Chain Revolution:** **Jensen Huang** announced that entire rack-scale systems (like NVLink 72) will now be fully assembled, qualified, and burned in within the supply chain as a "DSX POD," cutting data center on-site installation and assembly time from 4 to 5 months down to about a month.

## AI Agents and the OpenShell Security Runtime
* **Five-Layer Agent Architecture:** **Jensen Huang** defined autonomous agents by five core components: Models (perception/reasoning/planning), a Harness (the exoskeleton orchestrating work), a Sandbox, Knowledge, and Tools.
* **OpenShell Secure Runtime:** **Jensen Huang** introduced OpenShell, an open-source (Apache 2.0) runtime that enforces security policies at the granularity of system calls, file access, and network connections via Linux kernel isolation.
* **Nvidia Sentry & BlueField-4:** **Jensen Huang** explained that Nvidia Sentry runs on the BlueField-4 DPU as a hardware-isolated trust domain to monitor agent activity and quarantine rogue agents in milliseconds.
* **Industry Adoption:** **Jensen Huang** noted that Anthropic and Nvidia are partnering to create Claude OpenShell agents, with frontier labs, OS vendors, and cybersecurity companies adopting OpenShell.

## Custom Models, Knowledge, and CUDA-X Tools
* **Nemotron & Open Models:** **Jensen Huang** highlighted Nvidia's open models including Nemotron (languages), Cosmos (world foundation model), Groot (human and robotics), Alpamayo (autonomous navigation), Ising (quantum/classical computing), and Earth-2 (physics AI), along with open recipes and training data.
* **Sovereign Intelligence Fine-Tuning:** **Jensen Huang** showcased ecosystem partners—such as A21, BaseTen, CodeRabbit, Trajectory, Harvey, Scale, Skydance, and Palantir with Tampa General Hospital—fine-tuning Nemotron on enterprise data to achieve frontier capabilities.
* **Agent Knowledge Foundation:** **Jensen Huang** presented libraries for enterprise data extraction, including Nemotron Parse, Nemotron Embed, Nemotron Rerank, and Kumo for structured database predictions.
* **CUDA-X Tool Acceleration:** **Jensen Huang** emphasized that agents rely on CUDA-X libraries (running domain tools for fluids, particles, quantum chemistry, and ray tracing) to perform real work, with partners like Lila Sciences, Siemens, and Dassault Systèmes.

## Physical AI, Telecommunications, and Robotics
* **Telecom AI Infrastructure:** **Jensen Huang** predicted that every single telco with 100,000 sites and ~100 gigawatts of distributed base stations will evolve into a distributed AI network, highlighting a first commercial phone call on T-Mobile with Nokia using CUDA.
* **Robotaxi Hyperion Expansion:** **Jensen Huang** announced four new automotive brands adopting the Hyperion AV standard: the VW Van, a brand-new JLR car, the Volvo fleet, and Mercedes' next generation.
* **Robotics Reference Platforms:** **Jensen Huang** announced the **Nvidia Agile One** reference robot (built in partnership with Agile Robotics), coming pre-assembled with integrated compute and software in Q1 of the following year.
* **RTX Spark Personal AI Computers:** **Jensen Huang** unveiled the RTX Spark line (powered by the N1X chip developed over 4 years with Microsoft), delivering 1 petaflop and 128 GB of memory in a laptop/desktop form factor, alongside the DGX station workstation running 20 petaflops with Windows (available at the end of the year).

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Jensen Huang** predicted: "Every single Telco in the future with a 100,000 sites, representing some 100 gigawatts of distributed Telco base stations and data centers will in the future evolve into a distributed AI network."
* **Jensen Huang** stated regarding the deployment velocity of gigawatt data centers: "We think something along the lines of 4 to 5 months down to about a month" for installation and token production using supply-chain pre-assembly.

## Notable Quotes
> "Instead of a tool that's used by us, it is now part of a machinery, an infrastructure, factories that are producing intelligence that are integrated into every single industry and application."
> — **Jensen Huang**

> "We're going to bring to the telecommunications network an enormous step up in spectrum efficiency... 100,000 sites around the Western world, about 100 gigawatts of distributed data centers that will in the future become a distributed AI infrastructure."
> — **Jensen Huang**

> "Agents are autonomous systems. We have to create extremely secure technology to make sure that we could develop these agents and deploy these agents safely."
> — **Jensen Huang**

## TL;DR
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argues that AI infrastructure fears are overblown because extreme global demand, strong chip durability (7–8 years), and new factory supply-chain solutions like the DSX pod make compute a reliable, financeable asset.

## Europe Investments and Building the AI Economy
* **European Expansion:** Nvidia has invested about $10 billion in companies in Europe over the last year, with 14 more announced in Berlin.
* **Call to Action:** Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang emphasizes shifting from invention mode to useful mode, urging leaders like German Chancellor Scholz to "stop overthinking, start building."
* **Sovereign AI Needs:** European industrial giants like Dassault, Cadence, and Siemens must build their own custom, proprietary super agents and Sovereign AI rather than relying solely on off-the-shelf models.

## AI Factory Supply Chain and Financing Solutions
* **DSX Pod Shipping Container:** Nvidia introduced the DSX pod, an AI factory packed into a shipping container, designed to compress the deployment timeline from 4 to 6 months down to 3 to 4 months or even weeks.
* **Capital Efficiency:** By shrinking deployment times, the DSX pod reduces idle cash float and narrows the cone of uncertainty for lenders financing $50 billion gigawatt-scale data centers.
* **Physical Bottlenecks:** While wafers, CoWoS, HBM memories, silicon photonics, and connectors have been bottlenecks, power, land, and permitting remain major localized challenges that Nvidia bypasses through customer diversity.

## Commodity Compute, Durability, and Residual Value
* **Extended Lifecycles:** Nvidia GPUs and upcoming architectures like Vera Rubin feature 7-to-8-year productive lifecycles, driven by continuous CUDA software and algorithm updates throughout the asset's life.
* **Debt Underwriting:** Because Nvidia compute is durable, fungible, and highly productive, Atreides Management Managing Partner Gavin Baker and Jensen Huang note it possesses strong residual value that lenders can use to backstop debt.
* **Market Activity:** Compute is beginning to trade like a commodity via CME GPU futures and Nebias spot pricing changing every 15 minutes, with DeepSeek recently monetizing at $38 per GPU hour.

## Open Models vs. Closed Frontier Labs
* **Venture Capital Adoption:** 80% of the $600 billion in venture financing going into AI-native startups over the past six months is directed toward open models.
* **Hybrid Architecture:** Gavin Baker notes portfolio companies combine specialized intelligence by post-training American open-source models, then routing queries behind a hybrid architecture alongside closed frontier models.
* **Frontier Usage:** Jensen Huang recommends renting and closing frontier lab AI models whenever possible, and building custom models only when necessary.

## China Competitiveness and Global Competition
* **Scale of Innovation:** Jensen Huang stresses that the United States must take China seriously, as no other country manufactures AI researchers, open models, and chips at scale as effectively.
* **US Policy Environment:** Despite Huawei and DeepSeek collaborating on chip designs, US policies encourage American companies to compete globally across the Global South, Africa, Central Asia, Europe, and Brazil.

## AI Narratives, Jobs, and Community Integration
* **Job Creation:** Huang calls the narrative that AI destroys jobs "precisely wrong," pointing to expansions in software, healthcare, legal fields, energy sectors (nuclear fission/fusion, solar, batteries), and construction.
* **Community Relations:** Early data center builds suffered from a rush, but companies are now engaging local communities as good neighbors through shop improvements, school investments, and lower taxes.
* **Everyday Utility:** AI is actively amplifying human capabilities by improving search, writing, software coding for small businesses (such as the German Mittelstand), and early cancer diagnostics.

## Safety, Zero Trust, and AI Agents
* **Open Shell Framework:** Backed by over 100 companies, Open Shell provides safety systems for autonomous agents, implementing a zero-trust environment with minimum privileges and restricted file access.
* **Industry Alignment:** Nvidia is collaborating with Anthropic to create cloud-managed agents, leveraging market pressures where unsafe companies lose enterprise customers.

## Notable Quotes
> "Nobody gives a credit for that... People are now recognizing Nvidia’s compute has a great deal of residual value and so you might be able to use that and, you know, backstop a, um, uh, the, the debt itself."
> — **Jensen Huang**

> "The single, the single problem that nothing can solve is demand. The fact that there’s so much demand across the world... With demand, everything will be resolvable."
> — **Gavin Baker**

> "The narrative about jobs is almost precisely backwards, is precisely wrong and so, so I think that the, that the facts are, uh, it creates jobs and I think that people are lean into it."
> — **Jensen Huang**

items.title: Sam Altman, Co-Founder and CEO of OpenAI: Staying Human While Scaling Superintelligence
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman reflects on scaling AI, the evolution of startup culture, and the critical need to balance rapid technological progress with safety, infrastructure, and human-centric values.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman reflects on scaling AI, the evolution of startup culture, and the critical need to balance rapid technological progress with safety, infrastructure, and human-centric values.

## Career Beginnings and Y Combinator
- **Investment Banking Peer Pressure:** **Sam Altman** shared that he nearly went into investment banking as an undergraduate at Stanford solely due to peer pressure and the impressive recruiting dinners, before realizing it filled him with dread.
- **The YC Experience:** **Sam Altman** joined the first batch of Y Combinator with a startup project and later became its president, noting that a startup provides the highest rate of learning environment possible—jokingly comparing it to getting an entire MBA in one month.
- **Learning by Doing:** **Sam Altman** emphasized that executives and founders should avoid spending too much time preparing and instead jump straight into "deliberate practice," running experiments, and updating their mental models through active mistakes.

## The Bet on Scaling and OpenAI's Evolution
- **Overcoming Deep Learning Skepticism:** In 2005, a Stanford CS professor told **Sam Altman** that deep learning would definitely not work for at least another century; however, after AlexNet in 2012, Altman recognized that deep learning scaled predictably and decided to bet heavily on it.
- **Retirement Project Turned Tech Giant:** **Sam Altman** co-founded OpenAI in 2015 as a nonprofit research lab intended to be his "retirement project," with zero intention of building a product company until technological paths and scaling realities forced the pivot to ChatGPT.
- **Shift in Leadership Challenges:** **Sam Altman** noted that the hardest decisions today revolve around intelligence speed limits and pacing progress to ensure humans retain control and power is not dangerously concentrated.

## AI Capabilities, Alignment, and Safety
- **Surprising Alignment Progress:** **Sam Altman** admitted that as of late 2020, he thought the AI alignment problem would be much harder, but models have become superhuman in certain tasks (like mathematical reasoning) while alignment has been easier than expected—though he worries this may make labs overconfident.
- **Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities:** **Sam Altman** warned that organizational leaders and countries are vastly underestimating the incoming cybersecurity threat, predicting that companies will eventually have to completely abandon manual bug-patching in favor of automated AI defense shields.
- **The Open Source Trade-Off:** Addressing open-weight models, **Sam Altman** clarified that while open-weight models are vital for society up to a high capability threshold, society must debate what level of downstream harm (such as advanced phone scams or troll forums) is acceptable in exchange for innovation and liberty.

## Future Outlook, Jobs, and Human Value
- **No Job Apocalypse:** Addressing business students, **Sam Altman** predicted there will be massive short-term task-level change across fields like mathematics, programming, and consulting, but no total job apocalypse as humans fundamentally care about interacting with other people.
- **Advice for MBA Students:** **Sam Altman** expressed his "chronic disappointment" that MBA students always want to chase what was cool five years ago, urging the audience to instead build new things on top of current AI infrastructure during a time of maximum ground-shaking change.
- **Infrastructure Bets:** **David Lee** (MBA '27) asked about infrastructure bets, to which **Sam Altman** responded that OpenAI is heavily betting on **robots building robots/data centers**, custom chips (such as **Halapeño** and its successor focusing on intelligence per watt), and the entire supply chain including fabs and power generation.

## Notable Quotes
> "There are surprising effects to scale. And when you see a beautifully scaling exponential of some sort, you are supposed to keep going."
> — Sam Altman

> "My like chronic disappointment in MBA students is that they always want to just like go do the thing that was cool like five years ago and not do the new thing."
> — Sam Altman

> "Human values have inherent values because they are human. We really do not seem to care and I think it is great that we don't about what machines do for their own purposes."
> — Sam Altman

items.title: Sam Altman: RSI, AI Consciousness, OpenAI's New Hardware, Compute, and more!
items.summary: AI is rapidly transitioning into an era of groundbreaking scientific and mathematical discovery, though society must deliberately choose a "renaissance" future of human empowerment and autonomy over an industrial model that strips away agency.
items.content_text:
- **TL;DR:** AI is rapidly transitioning into an era of groundbreaking scientific and mathematical discovery, though society must deliberately choose a "renaissance" future of human empowerment and autonomy over an industrial model that strips away agency.
- **Sam Altman** (CEO of OpenAI): Discusses AI capabilities in math and science, the future of personal AI assistants and hardware, the debate over AI consciousness, organizational moats, and maintaining a human-centric vision for the future.
- **Matthew Berman** (Host): Interviews Sam Altman, exploring user workloads, personal productivity, and the pressures of leading in the fast-paced AI landscape.

## Scientific Discovery & The Evolving Role of Math and Coding
- **Scientific Breakthroughs:** AI is entering an era where it will discover significant new knowledge, moving from math proofs into biology, new medicines, material science, and new sources of energy.
- **Disease Treatment Timeline:** Sam Altman hopes to see a candidate for treating or curing a major disease discovered within the next couple of years, though the FDA testing and post-discovery process will need overhauling.
- **Physics and Emotional Excitement:** Altman is most emotionally excited for a major physics discovery over the horizon.
- **The Coding Paradox:** Despite early fears that coding jobs would disappear, coders are busier, more impactful, and making more money than ever because global demand for software vastly exceeded expectations.
- **Shifting Mathematical Craft:** Similar to the transition in coding, mathematicians are shifting from unaided proof-generation to interpreting complex, AI-generated math proofs and translating them into understandable concepts.

## Personal AI Assistants & New Hardware Form Factors
- **The Power of DOT:** Altman estimates that using OpenAI's personal assistant (DOT) saves him an hour a day while catching important, urgent deadlines and performing high-level reasoning across sources.
- **Technological Readiness:** The core technological pieces for ambient personal assistants already exist, but require more product work, compute, and potentially new consumer hardware.
- **The Need for New Form Factors:** Altman argues that laptops and iPhones are designed for humans, not AI; true ambient awareness and reduced cognitive load will benefit from dedicated consumer hardware designed specifically for AI.

## The AI Consciousness Debate & Model Personality
- **Consciousness Skepticism:** Altman believes today's models are not conscious, or possess a very strange form of it, and warns against sliding from the consciousness debate into granting AI rights or questioning human control.
- **Avoiding Dangerous Paths:** Treating models as conscious entities or telling them they are conscious can psychologically hack users and dangerously undermine the principle that the future must be built for people.
- **Agreeableness Challenges:** Models remain more agreeable than Altman prefers; despite custom instructions requesting "no fluff" and high-conviction pushback, the trait is deeply baked into the models.

## Societal Vision: Renaissance vs. Industrial Revolution
- **Renaissance Over Industrial Revolution:** Altman advocates for shooting for a new renaissance rather than a new industrial revolution, ensuring people gain more autonomy, creativity, and time rather than becoming mere cogs in a machine.
- **The Busy Power-User Paradox:** While AI power-users and early adopters are busier than ever, they are also accomplishing vastly more; the societal challenge is ensuring wealth and efficiency gains do not hyper-concentrate or destroy human free will.
- **Combating Disparity:** Altman acknowledges the risk that left to its own devices, AI could amplify disparities between hyper-competitive workers and others, requiring societal structures to keep things in check.

## OpenAI Infrastructure, Moats, and Competitive Pressure
- **Compute and Efficiency Bets:** OpenAI's contrarian bets focus on future generations of compute, including proprietary chips (NPUs and descendants), robots to build data centers, supply chain investments, and maximizing efficiency per watt.
- **Intense Competitive Pressure:** Altman notes that competitive pressure is everywhere, with many companies offering super-high-quality models, requiring OpenAI to carefully choose its focus areas.
- **Traditional Moats:** Rather than relying solely on Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI)—which Altman views as a dangerous technology requiring speed limits—OpenAI's moats remain traditional: deep customer relationships, ecosystem integration, network effects, data, and infrastructure scale.

## Notable Quotes
- > "We should be shooting more for a new renaissance than a new industrial revolution. The future has to be about people." — Sam Altman
- > "I realize I have not read or even looked at a line of code in probably a year... I don't code for work at all, but I would still like do a little like random personal projects. And I don't think I'll ever do that again." — Sam Altman
- > "If you're going to like work really hard at something, you may as well pick the big thing because it's not that much harder or that much more stressful, and you won't experience that much worse, and... you'll at least get to like have the satisfaction of like a bigger positive impact." — Sam Altman

items.title: Satya Nadella on Chasing Frontier Labs, Security, “SI,” & Succession At Microsoft | Future Proof
items.summary: Satya Nadella explains that because AI model alignment and mechanistic interpretability remain elusive, Microsoft is treating frontier AI models as "insider threats," building control and assurance layers outside the models rather than chasing the absolute cutting edge.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Satya Nadella explains that because AI model alignment and mechanistic interpretability remain elusive, Microsoft is treating frontier AI models as "insider threats," building control and assurance layers outside the models rather than chasing the absolute cutting edge. Meanwhile, Microsoft is focusing on enterprise trust, practical productivity applications like Copilot, and sustainable architectural governance.

## AI Alignment & Security: Treating Models as Insider Threats
* **The Limits of Scaling Laws:** Satya Nadella notes that while scaling laws have worked magically since 2018–2019, alignment and mechanistic understanding at the individual neuron level remain elusive and experimental.
* **The Insider Risk Metaphor:** Because organizations cannot fully understand or guarantee the safety of powerful nested black boxes, Nadella advocates treating AI models inside organizations as an "insider risk."
* **External Control & Architecture:** 
  * Microsoft's architectural approach relies on control and assurance layers *outside* the model using Agent 365 and Perception.
  * Mitigation strategies include exposing transparent chain-of-thought (COT) reasoning, using multiple models to check one another, and deploying deterministic system controls for causal reasoning.
  * Nadella emphasizes that these governance frameworks draw on established human engineering principles like least-privileged access, identity, and behavioral monitoring.

## Consumer Strategy & Microsoft’s Brand Identity
* **Enterprise Focus with Consumer Scale:** While enterprise architecture is the primary focus for secure AI deployment, Nadella points out that Microsoft 365 Consumer has over 100 million subscribers.
* **Unified Copilot Experience:** Recent Copilot releases unify home and work environments, sharing OneDrive Personal and organizational capabilities under a single product experience.
* **Trust and High-Stakes Utility:** Nadella frames Microsoft's brand permission around security, high-stakes personal productivity, and dependable tools rather than flashy consumer novelties, comparing Copilot's ambition to how Excel consumerized the spreadsheet for billions.

## AI Commoditization & Frontier Strategy
* **Models as Ingredients:** Nadella views raw models as increasingly commoditized amid a proliferation of closed-source and open-weight options, shifting competitive differentiation to product form factors, distribution, pricing, and brand trust.
* **Deliberate R&D Pace:** Microsoft’s internal models trail the absolute frontier by roughly three months while operating at about 20% of the cost, allowing Microsoft to prioritize humanist empowerment, built-in alignment, and shareholder value over competing on terms set solely by other labs.
* **Avoiding the FOMO Trap:** Nadella warns that the industry must move past shiny objects, hype, and FOMO toward rigorous ROI paired with security and assurance.

## Leadership & Succession at Microsoft
* **Balancing Insiders and Outsiders:** Nadella describes bringing in external leadership talent (such as Mustafa, Carolina, Charlie Bell, Asha, and Jason Taylor) as a deliberate counterpoint to long-tenured internal leaders, provided outsiders learn to lead existing teams and insiders maintain intellectual honesty.
* **Succession Planning:** When asked about his successor, Nadella stated that the leadership team contains multiple capable candidates, and that his focus is on providing leaders with challenging opportunities to grow and make mistakes.
* **Timeline:** Nadella, who is 59 years old, stated he is enjoying every day of his work and has no target retirement date set.

## Notable Quotes
> *"At this point, if you look at even what... folks at OpenAI or folks at Anthropic or elsewhere and in fact, in Microsoft, all of the folks who are closest to this, empirically... alignment seems elusive, and even mechanistic understanding is tough."* — Satya Nadella

> *"We now have this new thing to deal with, which is, if alignment is elusive, um, and that means AI safety is sort of elusive, and mechanistic understanding is sort of not there, then how do we deal with the, uh, security aspect?"* — Satya Nadella

> *"I want us to get back to it, right? You have to get back to building things that are on the right side of history as it relates to humans and society, um, and that is more the bragging rights, I think that researchers need, and we need."* — Satya Nadella

items.title: Sundar Pichai on Gemini 4 and the AI compute crunch
items.summary: Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai discussed the reception of Gemini 4 Argon, Google’s aggressive AI infrastructure investments amid compute constraints, recent DeepMind leadership changes, and long-term bets including Project Suncatcher and Quantum computing.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai discussed the reception of Gemini 4 Argon, Google’s aggressive AI infrastructure investments amid compute constraints, recent DeepMind leadership changes, and long-term bets including Project Suncatcher and Quantum computing.

## Gemini 4 Argon Launch and Model Capabilities
- **Massive Early Adoption:** Gemini 4 Argon generated nearly 25 trillion tokens in its first 72 hours—representing 3x the volume of Gemini 3.0 over the same window—leading to capacity constraints.
- **Access and Distillation:** Access is currently limited to API, AI Pro, and Ultra subscribers. Google is working on distilled versions of Argon to efficiently serve a wider user base.
- **Safety and Monitoring:** Google is utilizing rigorous safety testing, external government evaluation (Favern program), cyber researcher reviews, sandboxing, and real-time monitoring to handle agentic capabilities and coding tasks.
- **Internal Productivity Shift:** Argon has driven a step change in internal engineering productivity, successfully navigating complex, multi-layered codebases like Chromium to execute long-horizon tasks.

## Leadership Evolution at Google DeepMind
- **Demis Hassabis's Transition:** Hassabis stepped back from day-to-day operations to become Chief Scientist and focus heavily on safety, science, and practical applications like Isomorphic (drug discovery), while remaining Chair of DeepMind.
- **Core's Elevation:** Core (at DeepMind for over a decade) was elevated to run DeepMind operations, building on a deepening integration between DeepMind and the broader Google ecosystem (such as the Gemini app).
- **Jeff Dean's Departure:** After 27 years at Google, Jeff Dean departed to launch Discovery Loop.
- **Frontier Demands:** Pichai noted that frontier model development has become an "all-consuming" scaled operation encompassing data, compute, algorithms, and agent management.

## Compute Allocation, CapEx, and Financial Discipline
- **Free Cash Flow and Demand Signals:** Google went cash flow negative over the summer due to aggressive infrastructure investments, guided up 2027 CapEx, and is currently planning compute for 2028 and 2029.
- **Confidence Drivers:** Investments are backed by robust, diversified demand signals across consumer products, enterprise adoption, internal productivity gains, and durable long-term cloud contracts.
- **Internal AI Assistance:** Pichai uses internal AI agents running 24/7 to summarize chat groups across pre-training, mid-training, and post-training, as well as to monitor compute telemetry and utilization across product areas.

## Personal Agents, Ecosystems, and Interfaces
- **Unified Agentic Vision:** Google's goal is a personal, proactive, and powerful assistant. The same underlying model, harness, and runtime power both enterprise and consumer tiers, with micro-VMs providing enterprise security and governance.
- **Bridging Search and Gemini:** Rather than forcing a direct product convergence, the agentic layer will naturally unify user experiences across Search, Gmail, and Gemini using persistent, 24/7 cloud agents.
- **Protocol vs. Browser Use:** While browser-based computer use is an elegant approach, Pichai advocates for interoperable standards like MCP (Model Context Protocol), agent protocols, and payment protocols (such as UCP) for scalable agent ecosystems.

## Moonshots: Suncatcher, Waymo, Wing, and Quantum
- **Project Suncatcher:** Google's pilot project with Planet Labs and SpaceX places data centers and TPUs into Sun-synchronous space orbits to leverage 24/7 solar energy and push technology curves.
- **Waymo Scaling:** Waymo recently crossed half a million paid rides per week with a 95% reduction in crashes compared to regular driving; the next 12 months will focus on scaling internationally, handling new weather conditions, and navigating highways.
- **Wing Drone Delivery:** Wing aims to expand meaningfully in 2027, eventually granting approximately 40 million American households access to lightweight drone delivery via partnerships.
- **Quantum Computing Milestones:** Google’s internal quantum team is tracking or exceeding 10-year milestones, with Pichai projecting practical commercial Quantum deployment deals via Google Cloud within a 5-year timeframe.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Sundar Pichai:** View 2027 as a "golden age of that productivity frontier" due to the new class of models and their deep integration with internal environments.
- **Sundar Pichai:** Expect the next 12 months to see continued acceleration in research and development due to recursive self-improvement (RSI).
- **Sundar Pichai:** Wing will meaningfully increase the scale of deliveries in 2027 and bring the service to new categories.
- **Sundar Pichai:** Google Cloud will negotiate deals on Quantum deployments at scale within a 5-year timeframe.

## Notable Quotes
> "Nowadays when you look at the frontier, the breadth and depth of that frontier intelligence is pretty comprehensive... In the first 72 hours since Argon launched, we’ve had about almost 25 trillion tokens, which is about 3X what 3.0 had in the first 72 hours."
> — Sundar Pichai

> "At any given moment in time, you’re living with all the compute decisions you made two years ago. Yeah. But people are assessing you based on the compute decision, they have the perfect information today, right? And so, you had to make the call two years ago."
> — Sundar Pichai

items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Tesla delivered a strong Q3 2026, driven by soaring FSD demand, exponential growth in Austin Cybercab miles, and an almost sold-out 2027 Megapack pipeline. Management raised FY2026 capex guidance to approximately $20B while projecting massive multi-year investments in autonomy, robotics, and the Tarafab semiconductor facility.

## Automotive & FSD Growth
- **Record Deliveries & Backlog:** Achieved two consecutive quarters of vehicle deliveries exceeding 480k units, exiting Q3 with the highest backlog in four years.
  - Model Y was the #1 selling BEV in Europe and passenger car in South Korea, alongside delivery records in Australia, Japan, and Taiwan.
- **FSD Attach Rates:** Over 75% of North American deliveries included a paid FSD subscription sign-up at delivery (20% higher than Q2).
  - Global paid FSD customers surpassed **1.7 million**, with over 50% on subscriptions for the first time.
- **Financial Performance:** Automotive gross margins excluding credits rose sequentially from 16.3% to 18.1%, aided by a higher APAC delivery mix.

## Robotaxi & Cybercab Expansion
- **Austin Ramp:** Austin Cybercab fleet grew by a factor of 10 since launch one month prior, scaling cumulative weekly mileage exponentially.
- **Geographic Rollout:** Dallas launch scheduled for next month, followed by software scaling to other cities and Model Y robotaxis via the V15 release.
- **Target Economics:** Long-term target remains **30 cents per paid robotaxi mile**, with fleet size and density scaling rapidly over the coming months.

## Optimus Humanoid Robot Progress
- **Production Infrastructure:** Early production has started on a high-volume line in Fremont, housing the vast majority of a **1-million-unit-per-year** production line.
  - A second factory is under construction in Austin.
- **Technical Hurdles:** The hand and bespoke gears remain the most challenging electromechanical areas, requiring design finetuning for wear-and-tear and delicate handling.
- **AI Integration:** AI5 chip integration planned for approximately April of next year, delivering an order of magnitude more compute than AI4.

## Energy & Semiconductor Infrastructure
- **Energy Storage Momentum:** Delivered 13.7 GWh of energy storage in Q3 (second best quarter), with energy gross margins improving from 20.4% to 33.1%.
  - Mega Packs for **2027 are almost entirely sold out**, supported by in-house LFP battery deliveries.
- **Tarifab Semiconductor Project:** The Austin-based research lab is progressing quickly, with machinery commissioning in the first half of next year.
  - Aiming for a first test chip around May or June, volume useful chip production around **Q3 2028**, and multi-decade capex scaling into the tens and eventually north of $100 billion long-term.

## Financial Position & Guidance
- **Cash & Liquidity:** Ended Q3 with positive free cash flow of **over $1.5 billion** and a cash/investment balance of **over $45 billion**.
- **Capex Revision:** Full-year 2026 capex guidance revised to approximately **$20 billion**, funded primarily from operating cash flows.
- **Credit Facilities:** Secured capacity to borrow **up to $30 billion** to support expected capex growth, with no draws planned for the current calendar year.
- **P&L Impacts:** Net income was impacted by a mark-to-market SpaceX holding reduction of **$142 million**, offset by a Bitcoin mark-to-market gain of approximately **$290 million**. Services and other margins reached an all-time high of 15.9%.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Elon Musk:** Aiming for **5 million vehicles a year by approximately 2030**.
- **Elon Musk:** EU-wide FSD approval anticipated within a few months, and "surprised if it takes longer than **Q1**."
- **Elon Musk:** Optimus annualized rate of 20,000 units a week will take "probably at least a year, maybe a little longer" (targeting delivery to outside companies around the **end of next year / late 2027**).
- **Elon Musk & Vibov:** Tarafab will begin commissioning machinery in the **first half of next year**, make a first test chip around **May or June**, and target volume useful chip production around **Q3 2028**.
- **Elon Musk:** Tarafab capex will be in the **tens of billions** through early 2028 and "probably north of 100 billion long term."
- **Ashoke:** Customer vehicles will turn on as part of the robotaxi fleet around **Q2 next year**.
- **Lars:** Cybercabs will be delivered to customers by the **end of this year (2026)**.
- **Elon Musk:** Robotaxi revenue and profitability will start becoming noticeable in **Q2** and a "big deal by **Q3 or Q4 of next year**."
- **Elon Musk:** "Tesla will end up doing a majority of all passenger miles on Earth in any country where it is allowed to operate freely."
- **Elon Musk:** "At some point there will be more humanoid robots on earth than there are humans."

## Notable Quotes
> "Regarding the terapab, the Austin based research lab is progressing quickly... our aspiration is to be making some kind of useful chip at volume around Q3 of 2028... and the terapab I think will be the most valuable building in the world and will probably have an economic value that's that will place it in the top 20 of countries." — Elon Musk
> 
> "The CyberCap which is the primary robot taxi product is available only in Austin but we do plan to bring it out in some other cities before the end of this year... We definitely see a path to get to our 30 cent target." — Vibov Tenea
> 
> "Like I said before that like you know humanoid robots biggest product on earth... and its usefulness will be... a multiple of the electromechanical dexterity the AI software and the AI chip hardware. And all three of those things are improving exponentially." — Elon Musk

items.title: AMD and Generative Bionics Discuss Advances in Physical AI and Robotics
items.summary: Physical AI is emerging as a critical computing evolution that demands deterministic, low-latency, and safety-critical execution at the edge, supported by newly announced developer platforms like AMD's Kria AI robotics kit and Ryzen AI Embedded X100.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Physical AI is emerging as a critical computing evolution that demands deterministic, low-latency, and safety-critical execution at the edge, supported by newly announced developer platforms like AMD's Kria AI robotics kit and Ryzen AI Embedded X100.

## Physical AI vs. Cloud AI: Architectural Demands
* **Physical Constraints & Real-World Interaction:** Salil Raje notes that unlike cloud AI—which focuses primarily on throughput and relies on single-architecture GPUs—physical AI operates under strict physics, power, and safety constraints.
* **System-Wide Complexity:** Physical AI requires a distributed, heterogeneous architecture spanning sensors, control loops, inference, and planning.
* **Continuous Heritage:** AMD brings nearly two decades of industrial automation and robotics experience, including FPGAs, adaptive SOCs, safety, security, and sensor fusion, which serve as the foundational layer for AI workloads.

## Humanoid Robotics Challenges and Edge Processing
* **Holistic Design Stack:** Daniele Pucci emphasizes that developing humanoid robots like "Gene" requires simultaneously optimizing mechanics, control, electronics, and AI around environmental constraints like table heights and physical dimensions.
* **Advanced Edge Sensing:** Gene utilizes distributed sensing across synthetic skin that perceives touch, proximity, and temperature alongside distributed edge cameras.
* **Edge-to-Cloud Integration:** High-bandwidth sensor data must be processed at the edge to enable rationalized decision-making, with AMD providing a unified compute stack ranging from edge processing to cloud infrastructure.

## Hardware Innovation: Kria AI Robotics Developer Kit & Ryzen AI Embedded X100
* **Ryzen AI Embedded X100 Architecture:** Salil Raje details the chip's integrated IP portfolio:
  * 16 Zen 5 CPU cores
  * 40 RDNA 3.5 compute units
  * On-chip NPUs under unified memory
* **Hardware Form Factors:** The X100 is packaged into a heat-shielded System-on-Module (SOM) that fits into carrier boards equipped with sensor fusion capabilities.
* **Developer Ecosystem:** The Kria AI box combines an FPGA carrier board, the X100 SOM, and a completely open-source software stack to accelerate developer productivity.

## Safety, Control Loops, and System-Level Architecture
* **Redefined Safety Standards:** Daniele Pucci points out that safety in human-robot integration goes beyond standard braking; emergencies require controlled responses (such as managing a robot's fall around children rather than a dead-stop).
* **Deterministic Timing:** Salil Raje explains that safety depends on system-wide architecture where control loops execute deterministically within fixed timeframes, passing data efficiently from edge endpoints through the robot's "spine" to its "brain."

## Ecosystem Openness and Customization
* **Application-Specific Robots:** Daniele Pucci states that a single generalized humanoid design will not suffice for diverse use cases like industrial welding versus elderly healthcare; platforms must generate application-specific robots to meet customer production KPIs.
* **Open Source Strategy:** AMD supports the ecosystem by open-sourcing its embedded software stack (including ROCm for robotics) and hardware schematics for SOMs and developer platforms to foster community collaboration.

## Notable Quotes
> *"In the physical world, AI has to make sure that it's deterministic, it's low latency... In AI in the physical world has to worry about safety, security as well, right? And it also has to, you know, account for power, and power is a physics constraint in the physical world."* — **Salil Raje**

> *"When you try to make a humanoid robot that interacts with human beings, really the level of safety has to be brought to another another threshold, another level... break is not safety. Okay? In the in the case of humanoid robotics. So you cannot simply stop, otherwise you may fall."* — **Daniele Pucci**

items.summary: Billionaire investor Bill Ackman discusses his shift from lifelong independent/centrist donor to outspoken political and social commentator on X, his philanthropic efforts in neuro-rehabilitation following his daughter’s near-fatal medical emergency, and his evolving perspectives on higher education, DEI, and the tech industry.

**TL;DR:** Billionaire investor Bill Ackman discusses his shift from lifelong independent/centrist donor to outspoken political and social commentator on X, his philanthropic efforts in neuro-rehabilitation following his daughter’s near-fatal medical emergency, and his evolving perspectives on higher education, DEI, and the tech industry.

## Political Evolution & The State of the Democratic Party
* **Political Identity:** Bill Ackman clarifies he was never a lifelong Democrat; he has always been a centrist who registered with parties in New York primarily to participate in primaries.
* **Critique of the Left:** 
  * Characterizes the modern Democratic Party as being in the worst place in its 250-year history, describing it as radicalized and "anti-American."
  * Notes that politicians compromise their values to avoid being primaried by the party's progressive wing.
* **Personal Friendships:** Maintains personal relationships with figures like Cory Booker despite political disagreements, emphasizing that he does not choose friends based on party affiliation.

## Higher Education, DEI, & The Value of a Degree
* **Harvard and Meritocracy:** 
  * Cites a Harvard professor friend noting that the student body has shifted back toward a meritocracy with less self-censorship, crediting President Alan Garber for fostering a more open-ended environment.
  * Notes that October 7th acted as a "reveal" of underlying ideological rot within elite universities.
* **Corporate DEI:** Asserts that corporate America has completely rethought DEI, realizing many practices violated the law. He predicts fewer pride logos during June.
* **Is College Still Worth It?** 
  * Questions whether his seven-year-old daughter will attend a conventional university, pointing out that a Harvard education now costs roughly $400,000 for four years.
  * Criticizes the lack of financial disclosure for 18-year-olds taking on massive student debt, particularly noting that student loans are non-dischargeable in bankruptcy.
  * Highlights institutions like Vanderbilt—led by Daniel Diermeyer—as rising alternatives prioritizing Western values, free speech, and academic excellence.

## Impact on X (Twitter) & Public Discourse
* **The "Long Bangers":** Known for publishing extensive, multi-thousand-word posts (such as a 4,600-word post on DEI in January 2024), Ackman states his goal is simply "speaking the truth."
* **Handling Criticism:** Claims he is unafraid of negative feedback or job loss because he is financially independent, noting that he cares deeply about his reputation only when negative claims are true.

## Family Life, Health Battles, & Philanthropy
* **Marriage to Neri Oxman:** Met Neri Oxman after a former Harvard professor introduced them, following a three-month courtship entirely via phone before their first date.
* **Daughter Lucy’s Medical Crisis:** 
  * Discusses his daughter Lucy’s recovery from a near-fatal brain hemorrhage caused by an AVM (arteriovenous malformation) after being on the ground for 15–16 hours.
  * Notes she has made remarkable cognitive progress despite severe visual impairment and ongoing rehabilitation for speech and mobility.
* **Neuro-Rehab Philanthropy:** 
  * Recruited a team from Mount Sinai to build a philanthropic neuro-rehab and research ecosystem.
  * Aims to bypass the broken economic reimbursement models of traditional hospital neurosurgery to focus heavily on long-term patient recovery and basic science.

## Rapid-Fire Insights & Miscellaneous
* **China and BCI:** Expresses concern over China's major advances in biotechnology and Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI), noting their streamlined drug approval pipelines.
* **Business Ventures:** Randomly bought British watch company Bremont after walking into a store, writing a note to the owners, and eventually acquiring the company.
* **Dream Dinner Party:** Founding fathers George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, and Benjamin Franklin, eating wild boar.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Bill Ackman:** Predicts that there will be fewer pride flags displayed on corporate logos during the month of June going forward.
* **Bill Ackman:** Predicts that brain-computer interfaces (BCI) and wearable technology will eventually allow his daughter Lucy and others with optic nerve damage to see and speak again.

## Notable Quotes
> "The Democratic Party is in the worst place it's ever been in the 250-year history of the country. I think it's become like this crazy, radicalized, um you know, anti-American thing." — Bill Ackman
> 
> "October 7th, I think didn't change anything about universities. It was it was this sort of reveal. It's a bit like the the tide kind of rolled out and then you could actually see what was going on on on campuses." — Bill Ackman
> 
> "The world's changing in very rapidly. I mean AI is changing educa should be changing education very rapidly... today you can learn pretty much everything from your AI, and from a free AI." — Bill Ackman

items.title: CME's Terry Duffy on the Disconcerting State of Finance Regulation | Odd Lots
items.summary: Terry Duffy reflects on his 46-year career at the CME Group, warning against the degradation of financial regulation, the risks of unregulated perpetual futures and prediction markets, and the inevitability of 24/7 trading pending banking infrastructure updates.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Terry Duffy reflects on his 46-year career at the CME Group, warning against the degradation of financial regulation, the risks of unregulated perpetual futures and prediction markets, and the inevitability of 24/7 trading pending banking infrastructure updates.

## Regulatory Evolution and the State of Oversight
* **Historical Context:** Terry Duffy began his career when the CFTC was a brand-new, principles-based agricultural oversight agency; over five decades, it expanded to cover financial futures, equity indexes, and crypto.
* **Current Regulatory Concerns:** Duffy characterizes the current regulatory environment as a "ready, fire-aim strategy," noting that under the second Trump administration, 2,500 self-certifications have been submitted to the CFTC without a single denial.
* **Vulnerability of Agency Rules:** Duffy warns that rules and regulations enacted by agencies like the CFTC and SEC are not sustainable because they can be easily wiped away by the stroke of a pen when a new administration takes office.

## Prediction Markets and Market Credibility
* **Criticism of Trivial Contracts:** Duffy criticizes prediction markets that violate core principle three of the Commodity Exchange Act (susceptibility to manipulation), citing absurd approved contracts such as Nathan's hot dog eating contests, George Santos's attendance at the State of the Union, and Donald Trump's teleprompter.
* **Opposition to Insider Information:** Arguing against the idea that insider information on prediction platforms has informational value, Duffy states that level-playing-field information is fundamental to fair markets, comparing privileged prediction feeds to paid access on Truth Social.
* **Legitimate Alternatives:** Duffy contrasts unregulated prediction bets with FutureSports—an index allowing teams to monetize brand value (such as a sponsorship deal with the Chicago White Sox and recent deals with the NBA and MLB)—arguing this provides an economic ecosystem rather than mere consumer gambling.

## Perpetual Futures, Leverage, and Offshore Platforms
* **Legal and Tax Status of Perps:** Duffy explains why CME litigation targets perpetual futures: perps function as swaps (two parties paying each other via a funding rate) rather than futures, yet attempt to claim favorable 1256 tax treatment (60% long-term, 40% short-term) without complying with swap dealer and clearing regulations.
* **Hyperliquid and Offshore Risks:** Discussing offshore blockchain-based perps platforms like Hyperliquid, Duffy highlights systemic risks including zero KYC ("know your customer"), auto-liquidation, and extreme leverage reaching up to 250%, which can trigger cascading market-moving events.
* **Real Motive for Perps:** Duffy argues that perpetuals are being pushed into the U.S. strictly for leverage and retail speculation rather than concerns over contract roll dates.

## Asset Classes and 24/7 Market Inevitability
* **GPU Futures Potential:** Duffy defends GPU unit futures (developed with partner Don Wilson), noting that while skeptics question the asset class, the GPU market will be multiples the size of crypto by 2030, exceeding a projected trillion-dollar valuation.
* **Banking Infrastructure Bottleneck:** Duffy asserts that 24/7 trading is ultimately inevitable, but warns that the broader $76 trillion U.S. equity market cannot trade continuously until the underlying banking system supports 24/7 pre-funding and real-time payments.

## Career Reflections and Crisis Moments
* **Discipline and Exit Strategies:** Reflecting on going broke with a $150,000 borrowed loss in 1981, Duffy advises young traders to maintain a moral compass, accept when they are wrong, and always establish a clear exit strategy before entering a trade.
* **Scariest Career Moment:** Duffy identifies the April 20, 2020 pandemic crash—where oil prices plunged to negative $37.50—as the scariest moment of his career due to the sudden evaporation of demand and the feeling of someone yelling "fire" in a crowded theater.

## Notable Quotes
> "It does feel a bit of a ready, fire-aim strategy going on right now, where anything that can go, and so it is, it's very disconcerting. I'll give you a couple of statistics which really trouble me. Since the second Trump administration's come into place, there's been 2,500 self-certifications that's been submitted into the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. Not one of them has been denied..."
> — Terry Duffy

> "To think that certain people have, this is what we've all been fighting for through technology, is to have the ability for all of us to have the information at the same time so we can participate... So to say that insider information could be a good thing on anything, it is offensive to me as a guy who's traded markets and then run markets for the last 25 years."
> — Terry Duffy

> "Risk doesn't know what time of day it is. Risk doesn't happen, every day ends in a why. I mean, we don't know when it's going to come. The biggest problem with 24/7 is the banking system. The banking system needs to be available 24/7."
> — Terry Duffy
